notes: Variant assumption is a bilateral foot-supported seated cable row with an upright torso and a close-to-shoulder-width or neutral handle path pulled toward the lower ribs or upper abdomen. The direct evidence shows meaningful shifts by grip width and shoulder abduction: close/narrow rows better emphasize latissimus dorsi, while wide or high-abduction rows increase trapezius and posterior deltoid involvement. Rhomboids are included only as an explicit inference from grouped middle trapezius/rhomboid surface EMG plus scapular retraction mechanics; no isolated rhomboid fine-wire evidence was found. Erector spinae is included as support because it stabilizes trunk position against the cable pull, not because seated cable row is a back-extension exercise. Local meshes now exist for all visible muscles: BodyParts3D covers teres major, middle trapezius, rhomboids, posterior deltoid, biceps brachii, rotator cuff, and erector spinae; Z-Anatomy MuscularSystem100.fbx supplies left and right latissimus dorsi because BodyParts3D 4.0 English ISA/PART-OF tables did not expose a latissimus dorsi muscle mesh. EMG findings are interpreted as acute excitation, not direct proof of hypertrophy or injury risk.
